question: What Do You Think About Free Speech Laws In The United Kingdom?

answers.text: There's literally a plaque on the floor Like one of them drains there And it will say, And it will say, You can freely speak here but unless it’s one of them places where it’s got a little plaque on the floor You can't talk your mind
ESB Generally, as a citizen, I feel very much that I have freedom of speech
When you look at universities and things like that
I don't thinkthe laws are really strong enough
for people speaking in universities, because a lot of these speakers who go to universities, they don't sort of correspond to the student's sort of thoughts They get barred
With the Press today It's really hard because they just put it on the front page

and whatever they want us to hear it, they make us hear And unless you do your own research, you don't hear actually what's true And people are not able to say what they want to say or they say it but it doesn't get spread
It's absolutely fantastic. It's absolutely fantastic, on top!
I think globally, it's hard to establish freedom of speech on social media now
not an absolute right that we have
I'm still trying to figure out how in this new world [how] it should be used
We all internalize information we all personlize it and then we give it out into the world
People need to understand how much power that has, how much power they have with their freedom of speech
and also when they're being spoken to
I’ve been seeing some things that are trying to kind of squash the amount [of free speech] that we have currently
It's not good
We need more

We don't officially have it. Do we? Like the Americans It doesn't seem to be as much of a concern here as it is in America No, but I mean, the Constitution defends it in America It’s written in the constitution whereas we don't have any such I think we take it for granted -I can ask, where is it limited?
If you say things deemed offensive to anyone You can get in trouble
Could be religious groups, could be ideological groups
The government tries to play a sort of whac-a-mole with this
That tends to just make things worse
My personal opinion is we all need to be a bit more willing to be offended
and move on
